title: Math Linear Inequality class 10 ICSE Test
description: Math Linear Inequality class 10 ICSE Test 10 questions of 3 marks
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Solve the given inequation: 3x - 5 < 4, where the replacement set for x is the set of whole numbers (\mathbb{W}). Find the solution set.
questions.explanation:
First, isolate the variable x.
3x - 5 < 4
Add 5 to both sides: 3x < 4 + 5 \implies 3x < 9.
Divide by 3: x < 3.
The replacement set is \mathbb{W} = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...\}. The whole numbers strictly less than 3 are 0, 1, and 2. Therefore, the solution set is \{0, 1, 2\}.

questions.question: Solve the following double inequation: -2 \le \frac{1}{2} - \frac{2x}{3} \le 1 \frac{5}{6}, where x \in \mathbb{Z} (Integers).
questions.explanation:
Convert the mixed fraction: 1 \frac{5}{6} = \frac{11}{6}. The inequation is -2 \le \frac{1}{2} - \frac{2x}{3} \le \frac{11}{6}.
Multiply the entire inequation by 6 (the LCM of 2, 3, and 6) to remove denominators:
6(-2) \le 6\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) - 6\left(\frac{2x}{3}\right) \le 6\left(\frac{11}{6}\right)
-12 \le 3 - 4x \le 11
Subtract 3 from all parts:
-12 - 3 \le -4x \le 11 - 3 \implies -15 \le -4x \le 8.
Divide by -4. Remember to reverse the inequality signs when dividing by a negative number:
\frac{-15}{-4} \ge x \ge \frac{8}{-4} \implies 3.75 \ge x \ge -2.
Rewriting it in standard form: -2 \le x \le 3.75. Since x is an integer, the solution set is \{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3\}.

questions.question: Find the greatest integer which strictly satisfies the linear inequation 3 - 2x \ge x - 12.
questions.explanation:
Bring the x terms to one side and the constant terms to the other.
3 - 2x \ge x - 12
Add 2x to both sides: 3 \ge 3x - 12.
Add 12 to both sides: 3 + 12 \ge 3x \implies 15 \ge 3x.
Divide by 3: 5 \ge x, which is the same as x \le 5.
The values of x can be any number less than or equal to 5. Therefore, the greatest possible integer value for x is 5.

questions.question: Find the solution set of the following inequation: 2x - 5 \le 5x + 4 < 11, where x \in \mathbb{I} (Integers).
questions.explanation:
Split the double inequation into two separate cases and solve them simultaneously.
Case 1: 2x - 5 \le 5x + 4
-5 - 4 \le 5x - 2x \implies -9 \le 3x \implies -3 \le x (or x \ge -3).
Case 2: 5x + 4 < 11
5x < 11 - 4 \implies 5x < 7 \implies x < \frac{7}{5} \implies x < 1.4.
Combining both conditions: -3 \le x < 1.4. Since x belongs to the set of integers (\mathbb{I}), the valid integer values are -3, -2, -1, 0, and 1.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the solution set of the inequation 5 < 2x - 1 \le 11, where the replacement set is the set of real numbers (\mathbb{R})?
questions.explanation:
We solve the double inequality directly.
5 < 2x - 1 \le 11
Add 1 to all parts of the inequality:
5 + 1 < 2x \le 11 + 1 \implies 6 < 2x \le 12.
Divide all parts by 2:
\frac{6}{2} < x \le \frac{12}{2} \implies 3 < x \le 6.
Since the replacement set is Real numbers (\mathbb{R}), the solution cannot be listed as individual integers. It must be represented in set-builder notation: \{x : 3 < x \le 6, x \in \mathbb{R}\}.

questions.question: Solve the linear inequation 13x - 5 < 15x + 4 < 7x + 12, where x \in \mathbb{R}.
questions.explanation:
Split the inequality into two parts.
Part 1: 13x - 5 < 15x + 4
-5 - 4 < 15x - 13x \implies -9 < 2x \implies -4.5 < x (or x > -4.5).
Part 2: 15x + 4 < 7x + 12
15x - 7x < 12 - 4 \implies 8x < 8 \implies x < 1.
Combining the two results gives -4.5 < x < 1. Therefore, the solution set in \mathbb{R} is \{x : -4.5 < x < 1, x \in \mathbb{R}\}.

questions.question: If the replacement set is the set of natural numbers (\mathbb{N}), find the solution set of: \frac{3x - 1}{2} - \frac{x - 3}{4} \le 2.
questions.explanation:
Multiply the entire inequation by the LCM of the denominators (4) to eliminate the fractions.
4 \times \left(\frac{3x - 1}{2}\right) - 4 \times \left(\frac{x - 3}{4}\right) \le 4 \times 2
2(3x - 1) - (x - 3) \le 8
Expand the brackets: 6x - 2 - x + 3 \le 8.
Simplify: 5x + 1 \le 8.
5x \le 7 \implies x \le \frac{7}{5} \implies x \le 1.4.
The replacement set is Natural numbers (\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, ...\}). The only natural number less than or equal to 1.4 is 1. The solution set is \{1\}.

questions.question: Find the strictly smallest integer value of x satisfying the inequation: x - 5 \le \frac{5x - 2}{3} \le x + 2.
questions.explanation:
Split into two parts.
Part 1: x - 5 \le \frac{5x - 2}{3}
Multiply by 3: 3(x - 5) \le 5x - 2 \implies 3x - 15 \le 5x - 2.
-15 + 2 \le 5x - 3x \implies -13 \le 2x \implies -6.5 \le x (or x \ge -6.5).
Part 2: \frac{5x - 2}{3} \le x + 2
Multiply by 3: 5x - 2 \le 3(x + 2) \implies 5x - 2 \le 3x + 6.
5x - 3x \le 6 + 2 \implies 2x \le 8 \implies x \le 4.
Combined range: -6.5 \le x \le 4. The smallest integer in this range is -6.

questions.question: Given two sets A = \{x : -2 \le x < 5, x \in \mathbb{Z}\} and B = \{x : -4 < x \le 3, x \in \mathbb{Z}\}. Find the intersection of the two sets, A \cap B.
questions.explanation:
First, list the elements of set A based on its condition. Since x is an integer between -2 (inclusive) and 5 (exclusive):
A = \{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}.
Next, list the elements of set B. Since x is an integer strictly greater than -4 and up to 3 (inclusive):
B = \{-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3\}.
The intersection A \cap B consists of the common elements in both sets:
A \cap B = \{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3\}.

questions.question: Solve the following inequation and determine the exact number of integer solutions it has: -2 \frac{2}{3} \le x + \frac{1}{3} < 3 \frac{1}{3}.
questions.explanation:
First, convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions.
-\frac{8}{3} \le x + \frac{1}{3} < \frac{10}{3}.
Subtract \frac{1}{3} from all sections of the inequality:
-\frac{8}{3} - \frac{1}{3} \le x < \frac{10}{3} - \frac{1}{3}
-\frac{9}{3} \le x < \frac{9}{3}.
Simplify the fractions: -3 \le x < 3.
The integer values that satisfy this condition are -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, and 2.
Counting these values, there are exactly 6 integer solutions.
